data.arc: June 2025 marked the start of an AI‑driven data‑center expansion, driven by rising power demand, security threats, and new hardware like 36 GB HBM4 memory. Policy support in July accelerated massive builds and clean‑power deals, while August saw strategic cuts and hybrid‑energy initiatives to manage costs and grid strain. From September through March the sector experienced a surge of multi‑billion investments, global partnerships, and even orbital data‑center projects, but growing environmental opposition and a historic state ban in April introduced regulatory headwinds. By May 2026, geopolitical attacks added a new layer of risk even as corporations continued to launch large AI‑focused facilities worldwide. The narrative now balances rapid AI‑fuelled growth with mounting sustainability, security, and policy challenges.
